rules.title: Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with written notice of no-fault just cause termination including relocation assistance options and tenant rights to renewal offers. Relocation assistance must be provided as either a direct payment or rent waiver, with amounts specified by tenant status.
rules.key_value: 2 months rent; 3 months if senior or disabled
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord ends your tenancy for no-fault reasons, they must notify you of your rights and provide relocation help equal to two months' rent (three if you are senior or disabled). They must also offer you a chance to renew if the unit is rented again within five years.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador termina su contrato sin culpa, debe notificarle sus derechos y darle ayuda para reubicarse equivalente a dos meses de renta (tres si es mayor o discapacitado). También debe ofrecerle la oportunidad de renovar si la unidad se alquila de nuevo en cinco años.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all residential rental properties subject to no-fault just cause termination under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4).
rules.exemptions_text: No specific exemptions stated in this section.
rules.quoted_span: (c) Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause. (1) The landlord shall, regardless of the tenant’s income or length of tenancy and at the landlord’s option, provide relocation assistance to the tenant by one of the following: (A) The landlord shall provide a direct payment to the tenant. (i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice. (ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.

rules.title: Offer to Renew Tenancy After No-Fault Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: If a residential rental property is offered for rent within five years after a no-fault just cause eviction, the landlord must first offer the displaced tenant the opportunity to renew the tenancy in writing, provided the tenant notified the landlord within 30 days of the termination notice and provided contact information.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord rents out your unit within five years after evicting you for no-fault reasons, they must first offer you the chance to rent it again if you told them you want that within 30 days of eviction notice and gave them your contact info.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador vuelve a alquilar su unidad dentro de cinco años después de desalojarlo sin culpa, primero debe ofrecerle la oportunidad de volver a alquilarla si les informó que quiere eso dentro de 30 días del aviso de desalojo y les dio su información de contacto.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to no-fault just cause evictions under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4) and rental offers within five years of eviction date.
rules.quoted_span: (d) Additional Requirement Upon Termination of a Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause. If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant: (1) advised the landlord in writing within 30 days of the termination notice of the tenant’s desire to receive an offer to renew the tenancy; and (2) provided the landlord a mailing address or email address for the landlord to send the offer

rules.title: Voidance of Termination Notice for Noncompliance
rules.requirement: Any failure by a landlord to strictly comply with the requirements upon termination of tenancy under this Division renders the notice of termination void.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord does not follow the rules exactly when ending your tenancy under this law, the eviction notice they gave you is invalid.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador no cumple exactamente con las reglas al terminar su contrato bajo esta ley, el aviso de desalojo que le dio es inválido.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all terminations under this Division.
rules.quoted_span: (e) In addition to other remedies applicable to landlord’s failure to comply with this Division, a landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706. ... §98.0710 Failure to Comply with Division In addition to other remedies applicable to landlord’s failure to comply with this Division, a landlord’s failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall render void any notice of termination required by this Division.

rules.title: Tenant Remedies for Violations of No-Fault Just Cause Eviction Rules
rules.requirement: Tenants may sue landlords for violations of this Division and seek injunctive relief, damages including punitive damages, and attorney’s fees. Wrongful eviction damages are at least three times actual economic damages. Failure to provide relocation assistance results in triple damages.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord violates these eviction rules, you can sue them for damages, including triple damages for wrongful eviction or failure to pay relocation assistance, and get help paying your attorney.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador viola estas reglas de desalojo, puede demandarlo por daños, incluyendo daños triples por desalojo injusto o falta de pago de ayuda para reubicación, y obtener ayuda para pagar a su abogado.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to violations of this Division related to no-fault just cause evictions and relocation assistance.
rules.quoted_span: (a) A tenant claiming a violation of this Division may file an action against a landlord in a court of competent jurisdiction. (b) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money damages, including punitive damages, in a civil action against a landlord for a violation of this Division. ... (d) Any attempt by a landlord to recover possession of a residential rental property or any actual recovery of possession of a residential rental property in violation of this Division shall render the landlord liable to the tenant in a civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of not less than three times the actual economic damages. (e) Any landlord who fails to provide relocation assistance as required by section 98.0706(c) shall be liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages. (f) In the court's discretion, a landlord who attempts to recover possession of a residential rental property in material violation of this Division shall be liable to the tenant in a civil action for reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

rules.title: Regulation of Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with written disclosures before buyout offers, including tenant rights and relocation assistance eligibility. Buyout agreements must be in writing, include specific bolded statements, be provided in the tenant's primary language, and cannot waive tenant rights or be for less than relocation assistance amounts. Noncompliant buyout agreements are void.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord offers you money to move out (a buyout), they must give you a written disclosure of your rights first. The buyout agreement must be written, clear, in your language, and pay at least as much as relocation help. You cannot waive your rights in these agreements.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador le ofrece dinero para mudarse (un acuerdo de compra), debe darle una divulgación escrita de sus derechos primero. El acuerdo debe ser escrito, claro, en su idioma y pagar al menos tanto como la ayuda para reubicación. No puede renunciar a sus derechos en estos acuerdos.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all buyout agreements for residential rental properties.
rules.quoted_span: §98.0707 Buyout Agreements It is the purpose and intent of section 98.0707 to regulate buyout agreements to increase the fairness of buyout negotiations and agreements, to ensure that tenants who enter into buyout agreements are aware of their rights, and to prevent landlords from contracting around the legal rights and remedies available to tenants under existing law. ... (c) Requirements for Buyout Agreements. The landlord shall comply with the following: (1) The buyout agreement shall be in writing. (2) A copy of the buyout agreement shall be given to each tenant at the time the tenant signs the buyout agreement. (3) The buyout agreement shall include the following statements in bold letters in at least 14-point font in close proximity to the space reserved for the signature of the tenant: (A) You, the tenant, have a right not to enter into this buyout agreement. (B) If you, the tenant, are entitled to relocation assistance under federal, state, or local law, a buyout agreement for less than the amount of the relocation assistance to which you are entitled violates Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal Code and is void. (C) You, the tenant, may choose to consult with an attorney before signing this agreement. (4) If the tenant primarily negotiates the buyout agreement or lease, orally or in writing, in a non-English language, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an English and a translated version of the buyout agreement at the same time. A buyout agreement that does not strictly comply with all the requirements of section 98.0707(c)(1)-(4) shall be void. (d) Void Buyout Agreements. Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void. (e) No Waiver. The provisions of section 98.0707 may not be waived by a buyout agreement. Any term of a buyout agreement, lease, contract, or other agreement which purports to waive or limit a tenant's rights under section 98.0707 is contrary to public policy, unenforceable, and void.
